shower.thought: We spend decades learning how to be ourselves, and then we spend the rest of our lives unlearning it.
The people who say they don't care what others think are usually the ones most carefully curating that image.
You can't remember most of your life, which means you're essentially living with an unreliable narrator who happens to be you.
Nostalgia is just your brain editing out all the things that were actually wrong back then.
We assume silence means nothing is happening, but silence is where most of the important stuff actually occurs.
Your body is replacing itself constantly, but you still feel like the same person—which means identity might just be a story we tell ourselves about continuity that doesn't actually exist.
The moment you decide to change, you've already changed—everything after that is just proof.
We fear being forgotten, but we're all eventually forgotten anyway, which means the legacy we're so worried about securing is mathematically temporary.
Complaining about something requires you to have already accepted that it won't change.
The best relationships might be the ones where you genuinely forget to check your phone.
We're all just making educated guesses about what other people are thinking, and calling it understanding.
You only notice when something stops working, which means you live most of your life completely unaware of everything that's going right.
Boredom might be the only time your brain is actually free.
The things you're most proud of are usually the things you had to fail at repeatedly first.
We treat our attention like it's infinite, when we're actually spending the most limited resource we have.
If you had to explain your job to someone from 200 years ago, you'd probably realize how little of it actually matters.
Vulnerability isn't weakness until you decide it is.
Most of what we call wisdom is just pattern recognition from previous pain.
You've probably given advice that saved someone's life without ever knowing it.
The scariest part of trying something new isn't failing—it's succeeding and then having to keep going.

darkjoke.thought:
I told my girlfriend she was drawing her eyebrows too high.
She looked surprised.

My therapist told me to stop living in the past.
I said we'd talk about it yesterday.

I'm reading a book on the history of glue.
Can't put it down.

My dog has no nose.
How does he smell?
Terrible.

I said to my wife, "You never listen to me."
Or at least I think that's what she said, I wasn't really paying attention.

My grandfather said, "Your generation is too reliant on technology."
So I unplugged his life support.

I told my friend about my new diet where I only eat what I kill.
He said, "How's that going?"
I said, "Slowly. I'm not very athletic."

My wife accused me of not being romantic.
So I turned off the WiFi and made her watch me die inside.
I have a stepladder because my real ladder left when I was just a kid.

My dating profile says I'm fluent in sarcasm.
Apparently that's not what potential matches are looking for.
Who knew saying "You seem great" to everyone would backfire?

I tried to make a belt out of herbs once.
It was a waist of thyme.
My therapist says I use humor to avoid processing emotions.
Anyway, did you hear the one about—

Went to the cemetery yesterday.
People are dying to get in there.

I asked my dad why he named me after a car part.
He said, "Because we found you on the side of the road, and we needed to tow you home."

My friend said depression is just a mindset.
I said, "You're right, and it's a very crowded one."

I told my wife she was drawing her eyebrows too high.
She looked surprised.
The worst time to have a heart attack is during a game of charades.

I'm on a seafood diet.
I see food, I remember I can't afford it, and I go home.

My therapist asked why I always make jokes about my childhood trauma.
I said, "Because the alternative is screaming, and that really upsets the neighbors."

I gave up on New Year's resolutions.
Now I just wait until February and disappoint myself sooner.

My wife left me because I'm too obsessed with astronomy.
Good thing there are plenty of other stars in the sky.
Unfortunately, I can't reach any of them.
